note: From the 2026-08-05 MASAF register pass on comune Firenze (29 register entries). This was a deepening pass on an already-published city, not a new city. Leads failed only our evidence bar or the count; blocked can never ship as they stand. The 'off_cluster_currently_published' section is not a lead list, it is an observation about the live page for whoever next edits it. VERIFICATION PASS 2026-09-11: a brief asked this pass to re-verify seven old candidates from this file as if unpublished. Four (Monterey Cypress of Giardino Simone Weil, Strawberry Tree of Giardino dell'Iris, Chilean Wine Palm of Villa di Rusciano, Cypress of Villa della Petraia) turned out to already be live as flo_017, flo_020, flo_021 and flo_022, same names and coordinates, so this file was stale and never updated when those four shipped. Marked resolved below rather than deleted, so the mistake is visible. Do not re-dispatch them. VERIFICATION PASS 2026-09-12: worked the two remaining genuinely-Florence MASAF candidates from the passcheck brief's distance-ranked list (a Glicine at Via Pisana 130-132 turned out to be the SAME tree, same coordinates, as the already-blocked 'Wisteria of Via Pisana 130-132' above, nothing new there). The other two, MASAF 52 (Farnia, Mantignano) and MASAF 58 (Pioppo nero, Isolotto), verified clean against a second independent source (RAMI's own citizen-register pages) and were delivered to data/research/florence-verified.json as flo_025 and flo_026; both flagged for source disagreements on girth/height/age, both alive as of 2025/2026 updates, both confirmed-precision. Five more MASAF entries near Florence turned out to belong to neighbouring comuni (Bagno a Ripoli, Reggello) and are recorded below as wrong_city so nobody re-checks them. Also re-touched two open leads without resolving them: the Three Hackberries / Piazza Vasari alive-now question (evidence now leans toward felled, not spared) and the Black Pine of Villa Gamberaia access question (a promising but unverified 'pino laricio on the visit route' angle). Noticed but did not chase (would have been a fifth named candidate): RAMI's own Firenze listing carries a second poplar entry, 'Il Pioppo dell'Isolotto', distinct in name from the 'Il Pioppo dei Renaioli' delivered as flo_026; a future pass should check whether this is a register twin (same physical tree, two RAMI listings) before treating it as a fresh candidate. VERIFICATION PASS 2026-09-17: confirmed by machine (matching every comune=Firenze sheet_id in data/registers/italy-masaf.json against the live city file, blocked list and lead list) that the MASAF register for Florence is now COMPLETELY triaged: all 29 raw entries (27 distinct trees once the Piazza Vasari triple is folded) are accounted for, 23 published, 3 blocked (Observatory pine, Via dei Pepi Robinia, Via Pisana Glicine/Wisteria), 1 open lead (Gamberaia pine). There is nothing left to mine in this register for Florence; a future pass should not re-run a distance search against italy-masaf.json for this city without new register data. This pass also re-ran the distance-ranked candidate list a passcheck brief printed and confirmed every 'unmined' entry on it was one of: an exact-coordinate duplicate of an already-published tree (Olmo giapponese=flo_012, Pino bruzio=flo_013, Sughera=flo_002, Tasso=flo_001, Olmo del Caucaso=flo_011, Cipresso di Montezuma=flo_003 by matching girth 670cm, Cedro dell'Himalaya=flo_014, Cipresso di Monterey=flo_017, Corbezzolo=flo_020, and a 'new' 43.76266/11.26258 cypress that is flo_018 under different rounding), already-blocked (Robinia, Glicine), or wrong-comune by the register's own 'comune' field (Fiesole: bagolaro/cipresso/roverella; Bagno a Ripoli: cipresso/leccio; Reggello/Sammezzano: sequoia/lawson-cypress/redwood). Zero new register trees. Spent the rest of the window chasing the brief's own suggestion to search Florence's other historic villa gardens (Villa Gamberaia, Villa Bardini, Giardino Torrigiani, Villa La Petraia) for named veterans; see the new Petraia leads below and the updated Gamberaia entry. Zero trees cleared the two-source bar this pass; delivered nothing to florence-verified.json.

leads.why: RESOLVED 2026-09-17: verified and delivered to data/research/florence-verified.json as flo_027, 'The Hackberries of Piazza Vasari'. The Nov 2025 felling question is settled: La Nazione (lanazione.it/firenze/cronaca/ponte-al-pino-comincia-la-f7b338b5) states plainly 'il pino e gli alberi storici non saranno interessati dagli interventi', and a second La Nazione piece plus lafirenzechevorrei.it confirm two of the four Piazza Vasari hackberries carry the Region's monumental designation and were excluded from the felling. RAMI's own page for MASAF sheet 56 (ilregistrodeglialberi.it/16900) shows health 'Buona' as of 14 Oct 2025, weeks before the felling announcement. The three MASAF sheets (54, 55, 56) are folded into one entry per the register-twins rule; name corrected off 'Cascine' since the site is Piazza Giorgio Vasari in Campo di Marte, not the actual Cascine park 4-5km west. leads.name: The Black Pine of Villa Gamberaia
leads.why: MASAF 09/D612/FI/09, girth 364 cm. RE-CHECKED 2026-09-11, access still unresolved rather than cleared. The comune's own 2026 press release (comune.firenze.it, 'Alberi monumentali, sono 29 le piante sotto tutela') and intoscana.it both independently name 'il famoso pino nero di Villa Gamberaia' as one of the 29 regionally listed trees and confirm it is among the 14 privately owned ones, which is a genuine second source for existence and species (MASAF plus these two republications). Villa Gamberaia's garden itself is a real ticketed public site (villagamberaia.com/en, Grandi Giardini Italiani: Mon-Sat 9:00-19:00 in season, EUR 20), so paid entry alone would not block it. What still blocks it: the villa's own visitor-facing garden page lists its planted species (cypress, box, yew, oak, lemon, olive) and does not mention a pine at all, and 'the Villa is not open to public visits, only the outdoor gardens are' -- so it is not established whether the registered pine stands inside the ticketed garden circuit or elsewhere on the private estate nearer the villa building. RE-CHECKED AGAIN 2026-09-17, and the 2026-09-12 'pino laricio' angle is now RETIRED rather than merely unconfirmed: that quote came only from a WebSearch AI summary of turismo.it's article, and this pass fetched the actual page directly (curl with a browser user-agent, HTTP 200, 37 KB of real article text, not the earlier 403) and read it in full. The live article text describes the garden's history, the 225 m lawn axis, the cabinet de rocaille and 'il bosco di lecci secolari' (a wood of centuries-old holm oaks, an ensemble rather than a single collectible point) beside the lemon terrace. It contains no mention anywhere of a pine, a Corsican pine, laricio, or the Arno-valley-view sentence WebSearch had quoted. This is exactly the search-summary-invents-detail failure BRIEF_RESEARCH.md warns about (the Cyprus olive case): the AI summary manufactured a plausible, specific, citable-looking quote that does not exist on the page it was attributed to. Do not trust a WebSearch summary of this specific URL again; if this angle is worth pursuing further it needs a genuinely different primary source (an official garden map, a guided-tour description, or an OSM/aerial check of the ticketed-garden boundary for a large conifer crown), not another search of the same one. Access remains unresolved and this tree stays a lead.

leads.name: Further Orto Botanico trees on RAMI but not on MASAF
leads.species: Acer x peronai, Ginkgo biloba, Liriodendron tulipifera
leads.why: CHECKED 2026-08-22, still a lead, evidence bar not cleared. RAMI's own per-tree pages for all three (6486, 6489, 6493, registered 14 Oct 2021, updated 29 Dec 2024) carry ZERO measurements: no girth, no height, no age, and for ginkgo/tulip tree no coordinates either (only the maple has a GPS fix, 43.778719/11.262035, about 130 m from the flo_012 zelkova). English Wikipedia's Orto_Botanico_di_Firenze article independently confirms ginkgo and tulip tree are among the garden's species, which is a second source for existence/species only, not for remarkability: it lists them among dozens of species with no dates or measurements, unlike its treatment of the yew (1720) and cork oak (1805). More telling: the garden's OWN monumental-trees page (sma.unifi.it/vp-363), the same page that supplied the second source for flo_011-014, does NOT include ginkgo, tulip tree or the hybrid maple among its 8 named monumental specimens (it lists a newly-added Cupressus dupreziana instead). That is the institution itself drawing a line and leaving these three on the outside. The hybrid maple has one genuinely promising angle unexplored: Acer x peronai is described in Kew POWO and CABI-adjacent sources as one of the rarest European maples, with only about nine naturally-occurring wild individuals known, all in the Florence area, which would make a cultivated specimen in the collection historically/botanically significant regardless of size. No source found yet that documents this specific specimen's relationship to that wild population (age, provenance, whether it's a preserved wild individual or propagated). A search for the university's own dendrological collection inventory (a 'censimento globale delle collezioni' was reported launched August 2022, not yet public) or a scientific paper naming this specimen would settle it. Ginkgo and tulip tree remain thin leads with no remarkability evidence beyond bare presence; do not re-run the same RAMI/Wikipedia searches on a future pass without a new angle.

leads.name: Four Wikidata CC0 candidates (Q55742928, Q55742929, Q55742930, Q55742932) tagged as Florence
leads.species: Celtis australis, Quercus cerris, Cupressus sempervirens, Quercus pubescens
leads.why: CHECKED 2026-09-11: these are NOT Florence trees. All four carry catalog codes of the form NN/D575/FI/09, and D575 is the codice catastale for the comune of FIESOLE, not Firenze (Firenze itself is D612/FI/09, the code every other entry in this file uses). Their addresses (Terenzano-Compiobbi, Pian del Mugnone, Via del Bargellino, Torre a Buiano) are all in or near Fiesole, a separate hill town a few km northeast of Florence, reachable by ATAF bus in well under 30 minutes and a plausible day-trip candidate in its own right, but not currently a published city (no data/cities/fiesole.json exists) and out of scope for a Florence deepen pass. Q55742928 (the bagolaro with an image) is independently confirmed as Fiesole's own 'Bagolaro di Terenzano' via a RAMI page (ilregistrodeglialberi.it/14381). Do not fold these into Florence's candidate list again; if pursued, they belong to a Fiesole city brief (own verification pass, own four-candidate budget) or, if genuinely walkable from central Florence, an explicit day-trip entry with Fiesole named honestly as the place, per BRIEF_RESEARCH's day-trip rule.

leads.name: Five more MASAF entries near Florence that are not Florence trees (checked 2026-09-12)
leads.species: Cupressus sempervirens L. (x2), Quercus ilex L., Sequoiadendron giganteum, Chamaecyparis lawsoniana, Sequoia sempervirens
leads.why: CHECKED 2026-09-12, during a Florence deepen pass, by reading the 'comune' field directly off data/registers/italy-masaf.json rather than trusting distance-from-Florence-centre alone (the passcheck brief lists these by raw km distance, which does not know comune boundaries). None belong to Florence: a Cipresso comune at 43.753633/11.332725 (girth 510 cm) and a Leccio at 43.728556/11.31225 (girth 745 cm) both carry comune 'Bagno a Ripoli', a separate municipality southeast of Florence. Three more, a Sequoia gigante (girth 610 cm), a Cipresso di Lawson (girth 230 cm) and a Sequoia sempreverde (girth 840 cm), all three at Castello di Sammezzano near Leccio, comune 'Reggello', about 19 km away and belonging to a well-known separate tourist site (the castle and its park) rather than to Florence at all; also outside any reasonable day-trip transport boundary for a Florence page. Do not re-surface any of these five against Florence again; they would need their own city or day-trip brief for Bagno a Ripoli / Reggello / Sammezzano respectively, none of which are currently in scope.

leads.name: The Holm Oak of Villa della Petraia (near the garden entrance)
leads.why: FOUND 2026-09-17, following up on the brief's suggestion to search Florence's Medici villa gardens beyond what MASAF already covers (the MASAF register for Florence is now fully triaged, see the top-level note). ascuoladaglialberi.net's Tuscany monumental-tree survey, already used elsewhere in this file as a source, describes 'un gran LECCIO col tronco dalla circonferenza di 4 metri' (a large holm oak, trunk circumference 4 m) standing just inside the garden entrance at Villa della Petraia, opposite a downy oak (see next lead). NOT VERIFIED: this is one source only. A second attempt at a source specifically raised a caution rather than resolving it: aboutplants.eu's own Villa La Petraia article, read directly, says that in the late 19th century under Vittorio Emanuele II 'a great Quercus ilex used to host a terrace-belvedere' but that 'almost nothing remained of the great Quercus ilex', which may describe a different, now-diminished holm oak, or may mean the specimen ascuoladaglialberi.net measured is not the storied one, or may be the same tree under two different readings decades apart. villegiardinimedicei.it and italianbotanicalheritage.com's own Petraia pages, both fetched directly, list holm oak only among the park's general species with no individual measurement. No RAMI (ilregistrodeglialberi.it) entry found for this specimen despite a targeted search. Villa della Petraia is a Medici villa with free entry to its garden (state-run, per the villa's own site). NEXT PASS: search for a second source giving the same or a compatible 4 m figure specifically (a Musei Toscana or Polo Museale page, a dendrological paper, or RAMI under a Petraia-specific URL not yet found), or treat aboutplants.eu's 'almost nothing remained' as settling that this tree no longer stands as described and drop the lead.

leads.name: The Downy Oak of Villa della Petraia (opposite the fountain)
leads.why: FOUND 2026-09-17, same source and same visit as the holm oak lead above. ascuoladaglialberi.net: 'una parente QUERCIA ROVERELLA di trecento anni con una circonferenza del tronco di 4,5 metri' (a related downy oak, three hundred years old, trunk circumference 4.5 m), standing opposite the fountain from the holm oak, both near the garden entrance. NOT VERIFIED: single source only. No second source found with a matching or even a compatible figure; villegiardinimedicei.it and italianbotanicalheritage.com list 'downy oaks (Quercus pubescens)' only among the park's general planted species, with no individual specimen, age or measurement, and no RAMI entry was found. The 300-year age claim is exactly the kind of vague-source-repeated-vaguely figure BRIEF_RESEARCH.md wants kept vague rather than sharpened, so if a second source ever clears this it should ship as 'about 300 years' rather than anything more precise. NEXT PASS: the same second-source search as the holm oak lead would settle both at once, since ascuoladaglialberi.net describes them as a pair at the same spot.

leads.name: The Millennial Cypress in the park behind Villa della Petraia
leads.why: FOUND 2026-09-17. ascuoladaglialberi.net describes, in the park BEHIND the villa (a different area from the formal terraced garden), 'alcuni antichi cipressi malandati, di cui uno millenario dal tronco enorme ma dalla chioma ormai esigua' (several old, decaying cypresses, one of which is millennial with an enormous trunk but a now-sparse crown). This reads as a small group of ancient cypresses rather than one collectible point, of which only one is singled out as remarkable. A second source, aboutplants.eu, read directly, independently corroborates the general claim in its own words: 'la vegetazione e dominata da lecci e cipressi (alcuni di loro secolari se non addirittura millenari poiche, secondo alcuni Autori, potrebbero risalire all'epoca romana...)' (the vegetation is dominated by holm oaks and cypresses, some of them centuries or even a millennium old, which according to some authors could date to Roman times), again describing the park's cypresses collectively rather than naming one individual with a girth. NOT VERIFIED AS A DISTINCT, PLACEABLE TREE: the villa already has one MASAF-registered cypress live as flo_022 (girth 580 cm, in the terraced garden per its own how_to_recognise line, not 'the park behind the villa'), and it is not established whether the 'millennial' cypress these two sources describe is a second, different, more remarkable specimen or an exaggerated description of the same one. No girth or coordinate for 'the millennial one' specifically was found in either source. NEXT PASS: an OSM/aerial check of the wooded area behind Villa della Petraia for a single outsized cypress crown distinct from the formal garden's registered one, or a source (RAMI, a dendrological survey, a park map) that names or pins this specimen individually, would settle whether this is a genuinely new fourth-generation entry or the same tree as flo_022 described loosely.

leads.name: The Black Poplar of Via dell'Isolotto
leads.why: RESOLVED 2026-09-17: this is flo_026, 'The Poplar of the Renaioli', already live under the exact same MASAF sheet id (58/D612/FI/09). data/cities/florence.json's flo_026 cites a second source this lead's own search missed: ilregistrodeglialberi.it/17060-il-pioppo-dei-renaioli-pioppo-nero-firenze-fi-toscana (the RAMI/citizen register), so the two-source bar IS cleared and was already shipped before this lead was written. Do not re-verify or re-dispatch; check data/cities/florence.json for a MASAF sheet id before concluding a candidate is unsourced.

blocked.name: The Stone Pine of the Cascine Pratone
blocked.reason: Dead. Felled by the windstorm of March 2015 according to the Tuscany monumental tree survey. Hidde's rule: no dead trees as entries, however large. Girth was about 4.5 m.

blocked.name: The Wisteria of Via Pisana 130-132
blocked.reason: Private property. The comune's own list records the ownership as private and the address is a residential street number, so hard rule 10 applies: not open to visitors, do not publish.

blocked.name: The Robinia of Via dei Pepi 7
blocked.reason: Private property. Recorded as privately owned in the comune's list, at a street number in the centre, with no evidence of public access. Attractive location for a walk and still blocked.

blocked.name: The Myrtle of Villa La Stella
blocked.reason: Private grounds, and not a collectible point. The Tuscany survey describes multiple stems of up to 50 cm circumference in the gardens of Villa La Stella, with a Dante-era age it marks as unconfirmed. A multi-stemmed shrub on private ground fails both the access rule and the one-identifiable-tree rule.

blocked.name: The Plane Trees of the Cascine avenue
blocked.reason: Not a collectible point. Described in the Tuscany survey as the planes along the avenue towards the former racecourse, with girths to about 6 m. An avenue has no single place to stand and nothing to have seen, the same test that removed Barcelona's La Rambla planes.

blocked.name: The trees of Villa Torrigiani
blocked.reason: Access-restricted private garden. The Tuscany survey lists a fine ginkgo of about 6 m girth, decapitated by a German grenade in September 1944 and recovered, but states that visits require a reservation made by telephone through a private contact. That is not publicly accessible in the sense this site promises, so it does not ship. Worth revisiting only if the garden publishes open visiting hours.

blocked.name: The Monterey Cypress of Largo Enrico Fermi
blocked.reason: CHECKED 2026-08-22. MASAF sheet 16/D612/FI/09, girth 480 cm, height 16.5 m, locality 'Larco Enrico Fermi, 5'. That address is the INAF Osservatorio Astrofisico di Arcetri (Arcetri Astrophysical Observatory), confirmed via the observatory's own site: the grounds are not open to casual visitors, only to booked guided tours ('Per Prenotazioni vai alla pagina delle Visite Guidate'; entrance for guided visits is at Via del Pian dei Giullari 16). Fails the 'can they get in without asking anyone's permission' test. Not private land in the residential sense, but access needs an advance reservation through the institute, so it stays blocked rather than shipped as an open access tree. Worth revisiting only if the observatory ever states the grounds (as opposed to the telescopes) are openly walkable, or if the tree is visible from a public road/path outside the perimeter (not checked this pass).
